subject.title: Gateway process alive but event loop frozen — all HTTP requests silently timeout

question: Should this broader Gateway-freeze issue require both a proven supervisor recovery path and narrower root-cause fixes before it can close, or is a systemd watchdog recovery path enough?
rationale: Current main improves observability but not out-of-process recovery; choosing the close bar affects Linux systemd defaults, non-systemd platforms, and whether plugin/provider freeze triggers remain tracked here.

options.title: Require recovery plus trigger narrowing
options.body: Keep this issue open until a live-proven supervisor recovery path lands and remaining plugin/provider blockers are either fixed or moved to narrower canonical issues.

options.title: Close after watchdog lands
options.body: Treat a merged, live-proven systemd watchdog as sufficient for this issue and leave non-systemd or trigger-specific hangs to separate reports.

options.title: Split by trigger now
options.body: Close this only after creating or confirming canonical per-trigger issues for Feishu, active-memory, embedded-agent, and provider HTTP stalls.

recommendation.title: Require recovery plus trigger narrowing
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a live-proven supervisor recovery path lands and remaining plugin/provider blockers are either fixed or moved to narrower canonical issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans gateway runtime ownership and managed-service supervision, both areas where steipete has relevant feature-history commits.
